clue.text: Tricky question, part of quite a series

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzling question forms one episode of a quiz series.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or brain-teaser, a question meant to be tricky.

clue.text: Monkey oddly seen visiting burrowing rodent

indicators.note: visiting means calling in on, so the odd letters go inside the rodent

parts.note: a marmot is a burrowing rodent of the squirrel family

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions of the word seen

explanation.surface: A monkey has been spotted dropping in on a groundhog's burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes S and E from 'seen'; 'visiting' puts them inside MARMOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmoset is a small South American species of monkey.

clue.text: One may fear special constable ready to crack whip!

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for a special constable, a volunteer police officer

indicators.note: to crack suggests the word ready is broken up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: a cat is a whip, as in cat-o'-nine-tails

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman stands poised to crack a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaredy-cat is a timid person, someone given to being afraid.

clue.text: What a heavy drinker will do to exercise?

definitions.text: What a heavy drinker will do

parts.note: PE is physical education, i.e. exercise

explanation.surface: A question about what a hard drinker does when it comes to working out.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is to drink alcohol heavily and habitually, as a sot does.

clue.text: Source of persistent back pain that's found in certain writers?

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: An author's chronic bad back is put down to an occupational cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' takes P from 'persistent'. 'writers' are pencils, not authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is graphite, the material that makes the core of a pencil.

clue.text: Editor securing return of neat American book

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the editor's letters enclose the next piece
return of says the word for neat is read backwards

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: An editor takes back a tidy American volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is an archaic word for cattle, not tidy; 'return of' and 'securing' do the work inside ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Exodus is the second book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Mount donkey over from the East

indicators.note: reading from the East means right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone climbs onto a donkey after it arrives from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns ASSO into OSSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a mountain in Thessaly, Greece, piled on Pelion in myth.

clue.text: Go in front of stake and surrender

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake
to cede is to surrender or yield

explanation.surface: Advance ahead of the poker stake and then fold.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede is to precede, to come before in time or place.

clue.text: Splashing out one rupee, I'd kneel on this for devotions

indicators.note: splashing out suggests money spent freely and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone spending money freely says they would kneel down to pray.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a small prayer desk with a ledge for kneeling.

clue.text: Temporarily leave recreation ground

definitions.meaning: to leave a vehicle or a matter for a while, setting it aside
public open land for leisure, a green space in a town

explanation.definitionFit: Park as a verb means to leave something briefly; as a noun a public green space.

clue.text: Old Muslim official (namely, one employed by monarch)

indicators.note: employed by places the numeral after, as if working under the monarch

parts.note: viz is the abbreviation for videlicet, namely
one is the Roman numeral I
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the monarch

explanation.surface: A minister of the old caliphate is described as a servant of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high official in Ottoman and other Muslim states.

clue.text: Young ruffian I see held back by old golfer

indicators.note: held means gripped inside, so the reversed piece sits within the golfer

parts.note: Ben Hogan was a great American golfer of the mid-20th century

indicators.note: back says the pair I and LO are read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A lout is caught by a veteran golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ILO into OLI; 'held' puts it inside HOGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan is a violent young troublemaker, a lout.

clue.text: John Stuart's device for grinding pepper?

definitions.meaning: the Victorian philosopher J S ..., author of On Liberty
a small grinder for peppercorns and other spices

explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill was the philosopher; a mill grinds things like pepper.

clue.text: Boatmen finally eat in lock, being with it

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the lock of hair

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word boatmen

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Rowers finish off a meal on a canal lock and feel fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives N; N + DINE goes 'in' TRESS. 'lock' is hair, not a canal lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendiness is the quality of being fashionable or up to date.

clue.text: Huge old marines captured by English intelligence

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Ancient marines are taken prisoner by a vast English spy network.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous is a synonym for huge, very large.

clue.text: Being up in part of Yorkshire once?

definitions.meaning: being up on a horse, mounted and travelling on it
Yorkshire was historically divided into three administrative divisions, North, East and West

explanation.walkthrough: The Ridings were the three historic divisions of Yorkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding means travelling on horseback; a Riding was a Yorkshire division.

clue.text: Outshine former church leader for a start

parts.note: ex means former
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: for a start takes the opening letter of the word leader

explanation.surface: A previous church leader starts to outshine the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to surpass or outdo others, to outshine them.

clue.text: Arrangement bringing credit in problem game, strangely

indicators.note: in places the credit abbreviation inside the word for problem

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: strangely suggests the word game is jumbled oddly

explanation.surface: A setup that earns praise in a tricky puzzle game.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrummage is a rugby set piece, the arrangement of forwards packed together.

clue.text: MP and duke caught dipping into harvest

indicators.note: dipping into means plunging inside, so the pieces go within the harvest word

parts.note: to reap is to harvest
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A member of parliament and an aristocrat are caught joining the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: MP here is military policeman, not Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from their red caps.

clue.text: Roving son safe with a couple of chums? It's about the same

indicators.note: roving means wandering about, so the letters move into a new order
a couple of means two copies of the word chum

parts.note: a chum is a friend

explanation.surface: A wandering lad, safe with a pair of friends, finds it's all much alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' gives CHUMCHUM; 'Roving' rearranges it with SON and SAFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Much of a muchness is an idiom meaning very similar, nearly alike.

clue.text: What a defeated army does about entertainments?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
treats are entertainments or outings

explanation.surface: A beaten army is pictured enjoying its pleasures.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaten army withdraws, falling back from the enemy.

clue.text: Go one better than unelected party

parts.note: a candidate not elected is out
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Outperforming a party that failed to win seats.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass, to beat a rival's effort.

clue.text: Person interpreting end of Bible — one of unknown weight?

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word Bible

parts.note: x is an algebraic unknown
a pounder is one of a given weight, as in a ten-pounder

explanation.surface: A biblical scholar explains the last part of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of unknown weight' is an X-pounder, as a fish might be a ten-pounder.
explanation.definitionFit: An expounder sets out and explains a text or theory in detail.

clue.text: Italian girl in Wales disturbed by a right racket!

indicators.note: disturbed by means the girl's name is broken into by the other pieces

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name
din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: An Italian woman in Wales is upset by a dreadful noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sardinian is from Sardinia, an island region of Italy.

clue.text: Gangster penning note daughter provided with heading

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the gangster wraps the note

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster
ti is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A mobster writes a note to his daughter, putting a title on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Captioned means given a caption, a title or heading.

clue.text: Strong swimmer turning up with politician's book

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an otter is a powerful swimmer

explanation.surface: A powerful swimmer turns up holding a politician's book.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the book, the text, of an opera or musical.

clue.text: Iron container ultimately holding unusual cattle feed

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the pieces wrap round the word for unusual

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
odd means unusual

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of the word container

explanation.surface: An iron bin holds some unusual feed for cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R; FER, 'holding' ODD, gives FODDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is dried food such as hay given to livestock.

clue.text: Lazy person's papers on the French Resistance

parts.note: ID is identity papers
le is French for the
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A slacker carries papers about the wartime French Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone who avoids work, a lazy person.

clue.text: Run in a family member for criminal activity

indicators.note: in places the run abbreviation inside the other pieces

parts.note: a son is a family member
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A relative is brought in on suspicion of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberate fire-raising, is a criminal act.
